pick.name: Orca (stablyai)
pick.what: Desktop app: parallel Claude Code sessions each in its own git worktree, diff review, GitHub/Linear views, SSH worktrees, mobile companion, notifications
pick.why: Only mature Windows-native worktree orchestrator; MIT, ~108.6k stars, releases daily; brings your own Claude subscription
pick.free_limits: No paid tier. Anonymous usage telemetry (app opens, agent starts, OS/version; no file contents, prompts, paths or repo names); default state not stated; opt out in Settings > Privacy or set ORCA_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 / DO_NOT_TRACK=1
pick.install: installed; Windows .exe from onorca.dev or GitHub releases (no winget package documented)

alts.name: Built-in agent view + worktrees (claude agents, --worktree, /batch)
alts.what: First-party background sessions, each auto-moved into .claude/worktrees

alts.name: Claude desktop app parallel sessions
alts.what: GUI parallel sessions with visual diffs
alts.why: First-party GUI if you drop Orca

candidates.name: Built-in agent view
candidates.verdict: runner-up; wins once it leaves research preview or if you want no third-party app

candidates.name: Conductor
candidates.verdict: macOS-first, proprietary; no confirmed Windows build

candidates.name: Agent teams
candidates.verdict: experimental, off by default; no worktree isolation

decision: Orca wins on Windows: native app, MIT, daily releases, worktree-per-agent plus PR/diff review and phone notifications. Switch to built-in agent view if Orca's telemetry or hook load bothers you, or when agent view goes GA. Don't drive the same repo from both.

verify.note: MIT, ~108.6k stars, v1.4.243 dated 2026-10-28 (Latest, stable) all confirmed. The telemetry doc does NOT say telemetry is on by default; it sends no content/paths/repo names. Opt out: Settings > Privacy toggle or DO_NOT_TRACK=1 / ORCA_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1. README lists no winget package (installer .exe, brew, AUR only).
